{{Short description|Surface brightness model in astronomy}}
'''de Vaucouleurs's law''' (also known as the '''de Vaucouleurs profile''' or the '''de Vaucouleurs model''') is a mathematical function that describes how the [[surface brightness]] of an [[elliptical galaxy]] varies as a function of apparent distance from the center of the galaxy. The model is named after [[Gérard de Vaucouleurs]] who first formulated it in 1948.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Gerard Henri de Vaucouleurs (1918 - 1995)|journal=Bulletin of the American Astronomical Society|year=1996}}</ref><ref name="American Institute of Physics 2015">{{cite web | title=Gerard De Vaucouleurs | website=American Institute of Physics | date=2015-01-15 | url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/33930 | access-date=2017-06-22}}</ref> Other notable density profiles which approximately reproduce de Vaucouleurs's law include the [[Jaffe profile]] and the [[Dehnen profile]].

== Definition ==
de Vaucouleurs's law is a special case of the [[Sérsic profile]], with an [[Sersic index|index]] of <math>n=4</math>, and has the functional form<math display="block">\ln I(R) = \ln I_{0} - k R^{1/4},</math>or<math display="block">I(R) = I_0 \exp{\!\left(-k R^{1/4}\right)},</math>where <math>I_{0}</math> is the [[Surface brightness|intensity]] at <math>R = 0</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=de Vaucouleurs |first=Gerard |date=1948-01-01 |title = Recherches sur les Nébuleuses Extragalactiques |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1948AnAp...11..247D |journal=Annales d'Astrophysique |volume=11 |pages=247 |bibcode=1948AnAp...11..247D |issn=0365-0499}}</ref> Defining <math>
R_e
</math> as the [[Galaxy effective radius|half-light radius]] (the [[isophote]] containing half of the galaxy's total [[luminosity]]), the de Vaucoulers profile may also be expressed as <math display="block">
I(R) = I_0 \exp \left( -7.66925 \left[ \left( \frac{R}{R_e}\right)^{1/4} -1\right] \right)
</math>where the intensity at <math>
R_e
</math> is defined as <math>
I_e = I(0) \exp(-7.66925)
</math>.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Mazure |first=A. |last2=Capelato |first2=H. V. |date=2002-02-01 |title=Exact solutions for the spatial de Vaucouleurs and Sérsic laws and related quantities |url=http://www.aanda.org/10.1051/0004-6361:20011751 |journal=Astronomy & Astrophysics |volume=383 |issue=2 |pages=384–389 |doi=10.1051/0004-6361:20011751 |issn=0004-6361}}</ref> This can be confirmed by noting that<math display="block">
\int^{R_e}_0 I(r)2\pi r \, dr = \frac{1}{2} \int^{\infty}_0 I(r)2\pi r \, dr  .
</math>holds in general.

== Applications ==
de Vaucouleurs's law has multiple applications in [[Extragalactic astronomy|galactic astrophysics]]. It is primarily used for the modeling the surface brightness of elliptical galaxies and [[Galactic bulge|galactic bulges]], where it may be used as a tool in bulge-disk decompositions. de Vaucouleurs profiles may also be mathematically de-projected to yield expressions for mass distributions, [[Gravitational potential|gravitational potentials]], and internal stellar [[Velocity dispersion|velocity dispersions]], which may be used in [[Dynamical system|dynamical modeling]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Temi |first=Pasquale |last2=Brighenti |first2=Fabrizio |last3=Mathews |first3=William G. |date=2008-01-01 |title=The Mid‐Infrared Spectral Energy Distribution, Surface Brightness, and Color Profiles in Elliptical Galaxies |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1086/523668 |journal=The Astrophysical Journal |language=en |volume=672 |issue=1 |pages=244–251 |doi=10.1086/523668 |issn=0004-637X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Burkert |first=A |date=1993-06-13 |title=Do elliptical galaxies have r1/4 brightness profiles? |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1993A%26A...278...23B/abstract |journal=Astronomy and Astrophysics |volume=278 |pages=23-28}}</ref> Notably, however, though the de Vaucouleurs profile fits many elliptical galaxies very well, the specific Sérsic index of <math>n=4</math> likely does not hold significant physical significance as many elliptical galaxies are also well-fit by Sérsic profiles of index <math>3<n<10</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Makino |first=Junichiro |last2=Akiyama |first2=Kazuhide |last3=Sugimoto |first3=Daiichiro |date=1990-05-25 |title=On the Apparent Universality of the r 1/4 Law for Brightness Distribution in Galaxies |url=https://academic.oup.com/pasj/article/42/2/205/8078076 |journal=Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan |language=en |volume=42 |issue=2 |pages=205–215 |doi=10.1093/pasj/42.2.205 |issn=2053-051X}}</ref> As a result, recent galaxy light profile modeling studies employ the more general Sérsic profile as the de Vaucouleurs profile may introduce systematic errors under certain conditions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cardone |first=V. F. |date=2004-02-13 |title=The lensing properties of the Sersic model |url=http://www.aanda.org/10.1051/0004-6361:20031696 |journal=Astronomy & Astrophysics |volume=415 |issue=3 |pages=839–848 |doi=10.1051/0004-6361:20031696 |issn=0004-6361}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |last=Faisst |first=A. L. |title=COSMOS-Web: The Role of Galaxy Interactions and Disk Instabilities in Producing Starbursts at z&lt;4 |date=2024 |url=https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09619 |access-date=2026-09-14 |publisher=arXiv |doi=10.48550/ARXIV.2405.09619 |last2=Yang |first2=L. |last3=Brinch |first3=M. |last4=Casey |first4=C. M. |last5=Chartab |first5=N. |last6=Dessauges-Zavadsky |first6=M. |last7=Drakos |first7=N. E. |last8=Gillman |first8=S. |last9=Gonzaliasl |first9=G.}}</ref>
